Client hooks that read the route follow the same Suspense pattern. When the route's pathname is fully known, they resolve during prerendering and need no boundary. When the pathname depends on dynamic params not yet known, the hooks suspend wherever the component sits. A nav or breadcrumb in a shared layout, for instance, suspends while Next.js generates the static shell for any route below it that has dynamic params. Wrap the component that reads the hook in

Component state now persists across navigations.
With Cache Components, Next.js preserves routes using React's
mode instead of unmounting them. Effects clean up and re-run normally, but
values, form inputs, and scroll position are no longer reset when navigating away and back.
If your code relied on unmounting to clear state, you may need to add explicit reset logic:
: stay open when navigating back. Close them in a
: Effects that depend on dialog state (like focusing an input) won't re-fire if the state was preserved. Derive dialog state from the URL instead.
results (success/error messages) persist when returning. Reset in the submit handler or user action when possible, otherwise use a cleanup effect.
